correctness.rationale: The proof first obtains the negative graph-based logarithmic slope by ergodicity. Uniform graph marginals make near-kink events summable, so the normalized kink clearance d_n/D_n grows and yields a positive exact affine radius. Recurrence of that radius and the primary paper’s simultaneous all-interior convergence force eventual common branches for every initial pair on one sample-path event. Differences thereafter equal a positive constant times D_n, proving the sharp logarithmic exponent. Boundaries and all quantifiers have been reconstructed; standard-library exact rational checker provides supplementary finite examples, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The original natural family had a published qualitative synchronization theorem but no global exact pairwise decay law. Proving that any two interior points eventually remain on the same affine pieces for all future random maps is a structural fact that turns infinitesimal slope data into exact pathwise finite-distance dynamics. The sharp entropy-deficit exponent is mathematically motivated by the existing stationary-measure computation and provides a verifiable quantitative benchmark.
